claude.sample_unit: clinicians (hospitalist physicians, nurse practitioners, physician assistants)
models_evaluated: standard AI model for pneumonia, heart failure, COPD

links.outcome: Clinician diagnostic accuracy with vs without AI input, including biased AI and overreliance
links.effect: Standard AI raised accuracy 2.9 points over baseline; systematically biased AI decreased accuracy by 11.3 points vs baseline (95% CI, 7.2 to 15.5).
links.quote: Systematically biased AI model predictions decreased clinician accuracy by 11.3 percentage points (95% CI, 7.2 to 15.5) compared with baseline and providing biased AI model predictions with explanations decreased clinician accuracy by 9.1 percentage points (95% CI, 4.9 to 13.2) compared with baseline, representing a nonsignificant improvement of 2.3 percentage points (95% CI, -2.7 to 7.2) compared with the systematically biased AI model.

links.outcome: Clinician accuracy when shown systematically biased AI predictions (automation bias/overreliance)
links.effect: Biased AI predictions decreased clinician accuracy by 11.3 percentage points (95% CI, 7.2 to 15.5) vs baseline.
links.quote: Systematically biased AI model predictions decreased clinician accuracy by 11.3 percentage points (95% CI, 7.2 to 15.5) compared with baseline and providing biased AI model predictions with explanations decreased clinician accuracy by 9.1 percentage points (95% CI, 4.9 to 13.2) compared with baseline, representing a nonsignificant improvement of 2.3 percentage points (95% CI, -2.7 to 7.2) compared with the systematically biased AI model.

links.outcome: Whether image-based AI explanations mitigate clinician errors from biased AI
links.effect: Explanations with biased AI improved accuracy by a nonsignificant 2.3 points (95% CI, -2.7 to 7.2) vs biased AI without explanations; with standard AI, accuracy rose 4.4 vs 2.9 points.
links.quote: Although standard AI models improve diagnostic accuracy, systematically biased AI models reduced diagnostic accuracy, and commonly used image-based AI model explanations did not mitigate this harmful effect.

links.outcome: Clinician performance with AI assistance vs baseline in a vignette workflow, rather than standalone model metrics
links.effect: Standard AI increased clinician accuracy by 2.9 points (95% CI, 0.5 to 5.2); biased AI decreased it by 11.3 points, showing standalone metrics miss human-AI effects.
links.quote: When shown a standard AI model without explanations, clinician accuracy increased over baseline by 2.9 percentage points (95% CI, 0.5 to 5.2) and by 4.4 percentage points (95% CI, 2.0 to 6.9) when clinicians were also shown AI model explanations.
